title: The Broken PATH
description: A .bashrc line overwrites PATH with a single directory; fix it to append and restore the standard tools.
scenario: Every new shell on this box is half-broken: `ls` works in the current session, but any fresh shell claims 'command not found' for everything in /usr/bin. A previous admin added `export PATH=/usr/local/apps/bin` to /home/intern/.bashrc — which REPLACES the PATH instead of extending it. Fix the line so the custom app directory is appended to the existing PATH, keeping both the system tools and the in-house deploy command working.
symptoms: A fresh shell cannot find ls, grep or any /usr/bin tool
The custom /usr/local/apps/bin/deploy command must stay reachable
Login shells behave differently from the current session — the classic PATH-wipe signature
mission: Fix /home/intern/.bashrc so the PATH line APPENDS /usr/local/apps/bin to the existing PATH (export PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/apps/bin"), keeping system tools and deploy both reachable.

hints.title: = vs :=
hints.content: PATH is a colon-separated list. `export PATH=/usr/local/apps/bin` REPLACES the whole list; `export PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/apps/bin"` KEEPS the old value and adds yours at the end.

hints.title: Always reference $PATH
hints.content: Any correct PATH line contains $PATH somewhere on the right-hand side. If it doesn't, it's a wipe.

hints.title: Test like a fresh login
hints.content: `env -i HOME=$HOME bash -c 'source ~/.bashrc; command -v ls'` simulates a clean shell — if ls resolves there, real logins will work.

acceptance_criteria.description: the PATH-wiping line is gone from .bashrc
.bashrc now appends usr/local/apps/bin to the existing $PATH
a clean shell sourcing .bashrc still finds system tools (ls)
a clean shell sourcing .bashrc finds the deploy command
